title: Tensor and sheafification for modules over a presheaf of rings
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be presheaves [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $\mathcal O$-modules. Let $\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal G(U)$, with restriction maps induced by those of $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal O$, and let $\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G^\#$, $(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ be the module sheafifications, sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. There is a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules $\mathcal F^\#\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal G^\#\cong(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$. In particular, if $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\iota\mathcal G$ denotes $\mathcal G$ regarded as a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules by restriction of scalars along $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^\#$, then for every presheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O$-modules there is an isomorphism $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#\cong(\iota\mathcal G\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F)^\#$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: Define $(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)(U)=\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal G(U)$ with restriction maps induced by $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$, and $\mathcal O$. The module-sheafification maps are $\mathcal O$-linear and $\mathcal F^\#$, $\mathcal G^\#$ are $\mathcal O^\#$-modules by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Pure tensors therefore define compatible balanced maps on sections, hence a morphism $\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G\to\mathcal F^\#\otimes_{p,\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal G^\#$.

proof.text: Sheafifying the morphism of Step 1 and using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], which defines the sheaf tensor product as sheafification of the presheaf tensor, gives a canonical morphism $(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#\to\mathcal F^\#\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal G^\#$.

The pure-tensor map $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ extends uniquely to an $\mathcal O^\#$-bilinear map $\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$ by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension]. The universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] then gives a unique morphism $\mathcal F^\#\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal G^\#\to(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$.

For the composite on $(\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G)^\#$, precompose with its sheafification map from the presheaf tensor. Both the identity and the composite send a pure tensor $f\otimes g$ to the class of the same pair of sheafification sections, so they agree on the presheaf tensor; the unique factorization through sheafification in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] makes the composite the identity. For the other composite, precompose its associated bilinear map with $\mathcal F\times\mathcal G\to\mathcal F^\#\times\mathcal G^\#$; both maps are the original pure-tensor map, so uniqueness in [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] and the bijection of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] make this composite the identity. The same descriptions commute with restriction maps, hence the isomorphism is natural.

For the particular case, apply the isomorphism to the presheaves $\iota\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal F$: $(\iota\mathcal G)^\#\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#\cong(\iota\mathcal G\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F)^\#$. By [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] the identity $\iota\mathcal G\to\iota\mathcal G$ factors uniquely as $\iota\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\eta}(\iota\mathcal G)^\#\xrightarrow{r}\mathcal G$ with $r$ $\mathcal O^\#$-linear, and the underlying abelian sheaf of $(\iota\mathcal G)^\#$ is the abelian sheafification of $\mathcal G$. Since $\mathcal G$ is already a sheaf, $\eta$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves by the uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] ($\eta r\eta=\eta$ forces $\eta r=\mathrm{id}$); so $r=\eta^{-1}$ is a bijective $\mathcal O^\#$-linear map, an isomorphism $(\iota\mathcal G)^\#\cong\mathcal G$ natural in $\mathcal G$. Substituting it gives $\mathcal G\otimes_{\mathcal O^\#}\mathcal F^\#\cong(\iota\mathcal G\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal F)^\#$.
